CASE.focal_event: NVIDIA agrees to acquire Arm in a proposed $40 billion transaction

company.name: NVIDIA
company.profile: NVIDIA is a U.S. semiconductor and computing-platform company headquartered in Santa Clara, California. It designs GPUs and related systems and software for gaming, professional visualization, data centers and automotive applications. Its computing platforms combine processor hardware with software, libraries and developer tools, including CUDA for parallel computing. The company uses external manufacturers to fabricate, assemble and test its products rather than owning semiconductor wafer-fabrication plants. Its results depend on end-market demand, product mix and pricing, development and manufacturing costs, access to manufacturing capacity and the timely introduction and acceptance of new products. This general business description uses information available in its fiscal 2020 annual report; no later product launches, acquisitions, financial results or customer agreements are assumed unless included in the supplied article.

articles.title: NVIDIA agrees to acquire Arm in a proposed $40 billion transaction
articles.text: NVIDIA and SoftBank announced a definitive agreement for NVIDIA to acquire Arm in a transaction valued at $40 billion. Proposed consideration includes $21.5 billion in NVIDIA shares, $12 billion in cash including $2 billion at signing, a possible $5 billion earn-out for SoftBank, and $1.5 billion of equity for Arm employees. NVIDIA said it would maintain Arm's open licensing model and customer neutrality while combining its AI platform with Arm's CPU intellectual property ecosystem. Management expected the deal to improve non-GAAP gross margin and earnings per share immediately after closing. Closing was expected in roughly 18 months and required regulatory approvals in the United Kingdom, China, European Union and United States. The transaction had not closed.
